groups.reason: Recipients and vaults are selected by the payer; a failing recipient reverts the entire transaction. Gas limits and reverting endpoints remain service-availability considerations. Discovery settlement is bounded to 256 items and guarded against reentrancy; registry checks and exact transfers fail the entire batch on error.
Routing validation is deliberately explicit; unit, callback, conservation and compounding tests cover the changed branches.

The certificate registry exposes the expected interface ABI; bounty integration tests exercise it. Explicit interface inheritance remains an optional type-checking improvement. Discovery publication implements the same exact-object query; local EVM integration exercises the deployed ABI.

Both public routing entry points are nonReentrant; the callback regression confirms nested routing is rejected. Before/after balances intentionally enforce exact asset consumption. Malicious/rebasing settlement assets remain unsupported.
Timestamps enforce expiry, unbond and challenge deadlines, not randomness or truth. Deployment must account for the selected chain timestamp and finality rules.
